page: Amazon Web Services r5n.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Compute capabilities include instruction support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic hardware acceleration via AES. The system contains 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Local storage is not provided, meaning instances must utilize networked Amazon EBS volumes, which are supported by a 75 Gbps baseline network throughput. There are zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the instance's strengths in large-scale memory throughput and transactional operations. Uncached large-block read operations achieved 217.82 GB/sec, while write operations reached 96.29 GB/sec, both placing within the upper quartile of benchmark results. Similarly, database operations scored strongly at 21,748.64 operations, alongside PassMark extended instruction capabilities reaching 54,153.69. Multi-threaded processing demonstrates consistent middle-tier capacity, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 11,686.0, multi-core stress-ng at 54,183.31, and Redis SET throughput measuring 50.71 million operations per second.

A clear tradeoff exists in single-threaded performance. Single-core stress-ng (1,286.19) and single-core Geekbench (1,121.0) placed in the lower quartile, alongside weak single-threaded compression and decompression metrics. Additionally, LLM text generation latency is constrained, logging 40.57 tokens per second on smaller 135M models and 7.55 tokens per second on 7B models. From an efficiency standpoint, the instance balances massive memory footprint and network capacity against modest per-thread compute execution. The r5n.16xlarge is well configured for in-memory databases, caching fleets, distributed analytics pipelines, and large relational database servers requiring substantial RAM and network interconnects without local disks.
description: Amazon Web Services r5n.16xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz. Configured with 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores) and 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it delivers an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside a 75 Gbps baseline network interface. The platform lacks bundled local storage and GPUs. Benchmark tests reveal top-quartile performance in large-block uncached memory throughput (217.82 GB/sec read, 96.29 GB/sec write) and PassMark database operations, complementing multi-threaded capacity demonstrated by 50.71 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-threaded CPU benchmarks and LLM text generation metrics trail in lower tiers. The r5n.16xlarge serves memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory datastores, distributed data caching, and relational database systems requiring high network throughput.
